title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists and pay-per-click direct-to-consumer advertising
authors: Eisenkraft Klein D, Zenone M, Kesselheim AS
population: Paid search keyword advertisements in the US linked to the Ozempic.com website, estimated with the Semrush tool
funder: Dr Kesselheim's research was supported by Arnold Ventures. The funder had no role in design, conduct, collection, analysis, interpretation, preparation, review or approval of the manuscript, or the decision to submit.
authorConflicts: One author served as an expert witness for the Federal Trade Commission and in cases against Gilead and J&J.
result: An estimated $7.5 million was spent on more than 15,000 paid keywords over 2 years, generating 2.4 million paid visits to the Ozempic website. 1729 keywords (11%) contained the term weight and produced more than 358,000 visits, 14% of paid visits, at a time when Ozempic was not FDA approved for weight loss; Ozempic for weight loss cost $302,757 and Ozempic weight loss $188,626. More than 3500 keywords (23%) did not name the drug, including competitors' names such as Trulicity ($203,578) and Mounjaro ($113,668) and phrases such as Trulicity side effects. FDA guidance on social media does not cover search engines.
